text: Gold jumped about 3% to near $4,045 and silver about 4% to $51.90 as the dollar slid after Democrats won control of Congress.
Gold miners rallied before the open, with Barrick and Newmont each up more than 5% and Kinross up 6.8%.
The dollar index fell about 0.6% to a four-week low of 101.25.
The 10-year Treasury yield fell to about 4.90% as investors moved into bonds after the election.
Stock futures swung from an overnight drop to gains: S&P 500 futures were up about 1.1% and Nasdaq 100 futures about 0.4%, held back by AI-related stocks.
Bitcoin dipped to about $75,700 during the vote count, then recovered to about $78,200.
Silver funds lagged on Tuesday before this morning's rebound: AGQ closed down 3.34% at $44.23.
